sections.title: Compact Kähler surfaces with semipositive anticanonical bundle
sections.abstract: The authors classify compact Kähler surfaces with semipositive anticanonical bundle and resolve a Demailly–Peternell–Schneider question about blowups of the projective plane at nine points on a smooth cubic.
sections.claimed_result: A claimed classification of compact Kähler surfaces with semipositive anticanonical bundle, including the stated nine-point blowup consequence.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Compact Kähler surfaces with semipositive anticanonical bundle.
sections.caveat: One-version arXiv preprint; detailed proof dependencies were not assessed.

sections.title: p-curvature in non-commutative Hodge theory and the Kontsevich–Soibelman operad
sections.abstract: For smooth proper differential graded categories, the paper claims regular singularity and quasi-unipotent monodromy for the categorical t-connection using reduction modulo p and an operadic p-curvature result.
sections.claimed_result: A claimed proof of regular singularity and quasi-unipotent monodromy, with Jordan-block bounds and applications.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Smooth proper differential Z/2-graded category over C; additional assumptions apply to one application.
sections.caveat: Preprint claim; the reduction-mod-p and operadic arguments require expert checking.

sections.title: Cascade mechanisms for Navier–Stokes blow-up
sections.abstract: The authors analyze inverse and forward cascade mechanisms in dyadic models related to 3D Navier–Stokes, obtaining instantaneous or finite-time blow-up results in specified regimes and regularity classes.
sections.claimed_result: Blow-up mechanisms in Obukhov and mixed dyadic models, including finite-energy solutions in an energy-supercritical regime.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Dyadic models and related inviscid or forced systems, not the full 3D Navier–Stokes PDE.
sections.caveat: Model results do not resolve Navier–Stokes regularity.

sections.title: A proof of the Willmore-type conjecture in CP2
sections.abstract: The paper proves the Clifford-torus lower bound for the Willmore-type energy among closed Lagrangian surfaces in CP2 and constructs non-Lagrangian deformations that lower the energy.
sections.claimed_result: The conjectured lower bound holds for oriented closed Lagrangian surfaces of genus at least one, while unrestricted minimization is disproved.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Oriented closed Lagrangian surfaces in CP2 with genus g >= 1, contrasted with non-Lagrangian deformations.
sections.caveat: The theorem and counterexample concern different surface classes.

sections.title: The existence and uniqueness of magic-faced hypercubes, and applications to Khajuraho most-perfect magic squares, cubes, and hypercubes
sections.abstract: The paper proves existence in every dimension and a symmetry-based uniqueness theorem for order-two magic-faced hypercubes, with applications to most-perfect magic objects and a Weyl-group orbit statement.
sections.claimed_result: Existence in every dimension and uniqueness up to natural transformations, plus the orbit classification of most-perfect objects.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Arrays of 1,...,2^n in order-two n-dimensional grids whose two-dimensional faces share a magic sum.
sections.caveat: Broader impact cannot yet be measured from attention data.

sections.title: Extreme values of central L-derivatives and heights of Heegner points
sections.abstract: Using Soundararajan's resonance method, the authors obtain extreme values for central derivatives of quadratic twists and corresponding large Néron–Tate and Beilinson–Bloch heights.
sections.claimed_result: Extreme-value estimates for central twisted L-derivatives and consequences for arithmetic heights.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Normalized newforms, primitive real characters from negative fundamental discriminants, elliptic curves, and modular forms.
sections.caveat: Exact ranges and constants require the full paper.

sections.title: Resilience of rainbow Hamilton cycles in pseudorandom graphs
sections.abstract: The paper proves rainbow Hamiltonicity, enumeration, and percolation results for dense enough pseudorandom graphs under bounded colorings or conflict systems.
sections.claimed_result: Many rainbow Hamilton cycles and robustness under random edge retention under explicit pseudorandomness and degree hypotheses.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Bijumbled graphs, minimum-degree conditions, globally bounded colorings or conflict systems, and lower bounds on pn.
sections.caveat: Applicability to a particular graph family requires checking the hypotheses.

sections.title: Concentration of Regularized Sparse Random Matrices: Spectral Edge Bounds via Nonbacktracking Operators
sections.abstract: The paper derives variance- and cutoff-dependent spectral-edge bounds for regularized inhomogeneous sparse random matrices and an improved condition for vanishing errors.
sections.claimed_result: Extreme-eigenvalue and singular-value bounds using a nonbacktracking-operator framework for dependent regularized matrices.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Sparse inhomogeneous random matrices, degree regularization, and graph moment conditions.
sections.caveat: Extension to more complex dependencies is proposed rather than established.
